educational_binder.note: More advanced/structured than the other content types — from the `insurance-binder-builder` skill document (provided directly by user, 2026-08-07). Structured, page-by-page downloadable PDF-ready binders for lead magnets, client education, or pre-appointment materials. Not a sales piece.
standard_15_page_flow: Pages 1-3: Framing & Context — why the topic matters, the common advice most people hear, why that advice exists (fair and respectful)
Pages 4-7: What's Missing — what the common advice doesn't address, hidden assumptions, where people get confused, why confusion leads to flawed comparisons
Pages 8-11: Side-by-Side Thinking — control vs. growth, liquidity vs. restriction, risk exposure vs. guarantees, flexibility vs. optimization
Pages 12-14: Reframing the Decision — better questions to ask, who this may be appropriate for, who it is NOT appropriate for
Page 15: Educational Close — reflection, learning, optional next steps (no sales pressure)

tone_options.educational_professional: Third-person, formal, technical accuracy, comprehensive — best for financial professionals, high-net-worth individuals, business owners
tone_options.conversational_accessible: Second-person, simpler language, analogies, Q&A format — best for general consumers, skeptical audiences, first-time learners
tone_options.hybrid_recommended: Start conversational in framing, shift professional in detail sections, return conversational in application/close

non_negotiable_constraints: No promised returns — never guarantee specific percentages or outcomes
No universal claims ("this works for everyone", "always the best choice")
No attacks on other strategies, advisors, or financial personalities
Acknowledge tradeoffs — every strategy has pros and cons
Always include who the strategy is NOT appropriate for
Visual direction required for every page (never leave a page text-only for the designer)

cta_examples: Schedule a free strategy session at McFieInsurance.com
Get an independent insurance review from McFie Insurance
quality_checklist: Use 'participating whole life insurance' (not just 'whole life' alone in technical contexts)
Describe life insurance as an asset or financial tool — never an 'investment'
Include a CTA pointing to a strategy session or McFie's contact info
Use 'policy loan' not 'withdrawal' when referring to accessing cash value
'At McFie Insurance' appears no more than once per piece
No banned words/phrases (see knowledge/objections.md and phrases-to-avoid source)
Never promise specific returns or guarantee outcomes
Never disparage Dave Ramsey, Suze Orman, or other financial personalities by name — address ideas, not people
Never call IUL, VUL, or UL policies 'good alternatives'
